Article Title: From boy wonder to leader: Shubman Gill returns to the land of his firsts
Article Text:
Shubman Gill

AUCKLAND: New Zealand holds a special place for Shubman Gill . In 2018, he was part of the U-19 team that triumphed here. A year later, he made his ODI debut also on these shores. Now seven years after those two memorable ‘firsts’ in his cricketing journey, the 27-year-old is set to lead the side. From the eventful night in Mount Maunganui with the U-19 team to receiving his ODI cap from MS Dhoni in Hamilton, New Zealand will always hold a special place. Remembering these two events still brings a smile to the Indian captain's face."We won the U19 World Cup here. I have very good memories. I made my international debut here in New Zealand. Whenever I come here, I feel very good," said Gill at the pre-series press conference.The stakes, however, are much higher now. He is no longer the prolific young batter from Punjab trying to establish himself in international cricket. Now, he’s the man at the helm as India sharpen their preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup. In 11 months, the team will compete for the ultimate prize in the 50-over format. The fixtures leading up to the tournament — beginning with the New Zealand series — offer the skipper an opportunity to find the answers India needs."I think the more we play at different venues, the more experience we get, and that will help us in the World Cup. From the T20 series, we have seen that there has been good bounce here with the new ball, which has challenged both the bowling and batting teams. So, both teams will face good challenges, and it will be a good challenge for us too. It is a young bowling attack, but we have all the qualities to succeed here. Hopefully, we will learn and do well," Gill said.While India's inexperienced bowling attack faces a significant test, the batting line-up looks formidable and settled. Not much has changed in the team's batting composition since the 2023 World Cup, and stability is expected to remain a key feature over the next 11 months."For us, No. 5 and No. 6 are a bit flexible. Our top four are pretty much set, and we are all right-handed batters there. If we feel we need a left-hander at No. 5, we can use Axar bhai. Or, if we feel the platform has been set for KL bhai to go out and play, we will decide according to the situation at that given point. The number of overs remaining and the position we are in matter more than fixed No. 5 and No. 6 positions.Injury-prone Hardik Pandya remains the crucial missing piece. However, even in his absence, the consistency of the established top four — Gill, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer — leaves the captain with only the No. 5 and No. 6 positions to figure out. The decision, though, is less about personnel and more about the demands of a particular match situation."We are definitely very happy with our top order and middle order. If Hardik bhai comes in, then our No. 7 and No. 8 positions are also sorted, and we look like a much more balanced team in terms of our batting," Gill explained.Gill echoed head coach Gautam Gambhir's sentiments about the challenges posed by an inexperienced bowling attack, particularly in the absence of Jasprit Bumrah, Pandya and Prasidh Krishna. However, he sees the situation as an opportunity for the younger players to grow in confidence. Gurnoor Brar, Auqib Nabi, Anshul Kamboj and Arshdeep Singh, along with Nitish Kumar Reddy (for the first ODI only), are India's options. Gill believes the squad has the ability to "defeat any team in any condition.”"I feel that any Indian team that steps onto the ground is capable of defeating any team. Young players will gain a lot of confidence if they perform here. We will also gain confidence that if, for any reason, we don't have the team we want for the World Cup, our squad can still defeat any team in any condition. In that context, if we win the series here, it will be a big confidence booster for us," Gill said.Even as he plans for the series and next year's World Cup, Gill has ensured that the bigger picture does not distract him from his batting or his preparation for each fixture. The Indian captain arrived in Auckland well ahead of the series, accompanied by Brar, to begin preparations for the long tour. The focus now shifts to translating those hours in the nets into performances in the middle.The flashy youngster of 2018, with conspicuous streaks of colour in his hair, now carries the expectations of more than a billion people on his shoulders. The boy-wonder-turned-leader is focused on adding another memorable chapter to his New Zealand story."Hopefully, when we go back after a month, we will take a lot more good memories from here."
Article Summary: Shubman Gill will captain India in their ODI series against New Zealand. The 27-year-old was part of the U-19 team that won the World Cup in New Zealand in 2018. He also made his ODI debut in the same country a year later. India are preparing for the 2027 ODI World Cup.

Article Title: Cutting the angles: India's key to fielding success in Auckland
Article Text:
Virat Kohli (left) and Arshdeep Singh during India's fielding session at Eden Park

AUCKLAND: The Eden Park outfield was buzzing with activity as soon as the Indian cricket team got down to business ahead of the first ODI of the five-match series against New Zealand. Divided into groups of four, the players ran between two equidistant cones placed across the ground and intercepted deliveries fired by fielding coach Subhadeep Ghosh and other members of the support staff.The plan was simple: players were asked to call clearly and loudly while approaching the ball, and whoever reached it first had to fire it back to the thrower. The drill lasted around 30 minutes, emphasising the importance of running in straight lines, even when approaching the ball from different angles. The idea was to help players familiarise themselves with the ground's dimensions, which differ from those they are accustomed to.That is where the challenge lies in Auckland. The floodlights are different, the dimensions could feel unfamiliar, and ground fielding could become tricky, with plenty of opportunities to take twos in the deeper pockets.Former India fielding coach R Sridhar, who was with the team during its last tour, says Auckland's dimensions are different and challenging, making the concept of "cutting the angles" particularly important."Cutting the angle means running in straight lines. Simple. You assess the speed of the ball and the dimensions, and then you run towards the ball in a straight line. Awareness, the ability to run and take off quickly—all these things are the challenges," Sridhar told TOI.Other factors, such as wind, cold conditions and the match start time, will also come into play. However, the team has travelled extensively and should be equipped to deal with these variables. Having had just one training session before taking the field on Wednesday, adapting quickly to Eden Park will be crucial.Fielding is one area where India would want to put its best foot forward in the upcoming series, particularly with "catching efficiency" becoming an increasingly important metric.While India's fielding standards are generally better in ODIs than in T20Is and Tests, the team no longer has the watertight look it once did. In the 18 ODIs played since the change of captaincy in the format, beginning with the tour of Australia last year, India have dropped 27 catches, recording a below-par catching efficiency of 77.5%.Kuldeep Yadav has dropped five catches in the 11 matches he has played, while KL Rahul is second on the unwanted list with four drops in 16 games. Interestingly, Rohit Sharma has taken the most catches among Indian players in those 18 matches, topping the list with 15 catches and just two drops.Eden Park will be the first stop on the tour, which will then move to windy Wellington and Seddon Park in Hamilton before the five-match ODI series culminates at the picturesque Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui."Each venue has its own set of challenges. There is wind in Wellington, and different dimensions in Auckland—where the country side is bigger—but Bay Oval should be fine. It is on the open side, but conditions will be fine for adjustment," Sridhar said.On addressing India's fielding lapses, Sridhar emphasised that there is no one-size-fits-all approach to preparation. He believes the experience within the ODI squad will help the players navigate the challenges."Each player will be different. Preparation volume depends on the player's mental state, what the player needs at that point, and what he has done before. So there is a lot of basis in volume. You just can't go blindly and say everybody has to do this volume. It doesn't work that way. In ODIs, there is a lot of experience. You have Rohit, Virat, Gill. All of them have played there before. I'm sure they will do well too," said Sridhar.
Article Summary: Fielding is one area where India would want to put its best foot forward in the upcoming series. Former India fielding coach R Sridhar, who was with the team during its last tour, says Auckland's dimensions are different and challenging. The team has travelled extensively and should be equipped to deal with these variables.

Article Title: Why India's 99th Grandmaster had to do it twice: The latest mystery of Indian chess, VS Rathanvel
Article Text:
VS Rathanvel, India's 99th Grandmaster

What went wrong?

The strange part and FIDE's stance on titles

The weight of an announcement

Doing it again

NEW DELHI: Last July, the congratulations arrived all at once. Reports and chess pages across India carried the same news that VS Rathanvel, a 25-year-old from Coimbatore, had crossed 2500 at the Guwahati Smart City International Open and become the country's 99th Grandmaster (GM). It looked as if his four-year wait had just ended.Rathanvel had finished his norms by 2022. What he lacked was a FIDE standard rating of 2500. Throughout this period, he had been stuck in the high 2490s, and by his own count had reached the edge of 2500 "probably 3-4 times"."You know that feel where you know you're worthy of it, but somehow you're not still getting there," Rathanvel had told TimesofIndia.com after what he, along with many others, believed would be the moment he finally secured the GM title Then, the August rating list came out, and surprisingly, his rating hadn't improved. With his rating still below 2500, Rathanvel was still not a Grandmaster.In the month of July, Rathanvel, rated 2492 at that time, had gone to Assam, needing eight points in FIDE standard ratings to meet the criteria of becoming a Grandmaster.He played two back-to-back opens in Assam, the Ayodhana International (six games) and the Guwahati Smart City Open (five), seeded first and second.Nevertheless, he didn't play all the games there. He took zero-point byes in some rounds, which kept his score low and kept the Swiss pairings feeding him lower-rated opponents.He won all 11 games, with ten of his opponents rated between 1451 and 1625 and one unrated.Each win against the rated players was worth only +0.8 because FIDE caps the rating gap at 400 points, and ten of them added up to exactly the eight points he needed to go from 2492 to 2500.In Ayodhana International, he skipped four rounds. And in Guwahati Smart City Open, he chose not to participate in five games. It was perhaps a smart move from Rathanvel.His performance ratings in the two events, 2225 and 2299, were both below his own rating as he finished 77th and 246th in those tournaments, respectively. But a top finish was never on the agenda, as he just needed eight points to qualify for the GM title.He had achieved it, and it felt as if India had gotten its 99th GM.Both tournaments were rated. Together, over 400 participants each at Ayodhana and Guwahati Open had their ratings updated. Rathanvel's rating, however, stayed the same.Unlike the Tamil Nadu-based player, his opponents were in the updated rating list, but each of them had one game fewer than they actually played against rated opponents, the missing game being the one against Rathanvel.Therefore, it can be concluded that all games played in those tournaments were counted, except for those involving Rathanvel."I have no idea (why it happened)," Rathanvel told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. "FIDE and the Indian Chess Federation (AICF) may have even had some discussion. I am not sure what happened. I was also not able to get satisfactory responses."The current rules follow the FIDE Title Regulations effective from 1 January 2024, published in the FIDE Handbook under the Qualification Commission’s International Title Regulations, in the section on norm-based titles (clause 1.4).Clause 1.4.2 lists what FIDE refuses to count towards a title. Games against opponents who do not belong to FIDE federations do not count (players with the “FID” federation are accepted but are not treated as foreign players). Games against unrated players who score zero against rated opponents in round robins do not count. Neither do games decided by forfeit, adjudication or any means other than over-the-board play, although other games, once started, are counted.A whole tournament can also be thrown out if “changes are made which have the effect of benefitting one or more players”, for example by altering the number of rounds, or the order of rounds, or “providing particular opponents, not otherwise participating in the event”.The formats allowed in title tournaments are Swiss, round robin, double round robin and knockout, and any other format needs the prior approval of the Qualification Commission Chairperson. The Qualification Commission is described as the “final judging unit” for titles, so it decides whether a result falls under any of these.The news was out that he was India's 99th GM, while, in reality, FIDE didn't approve it. "People had already made an announcement that I was the 99th GM," he added. "Every media channel covered it."There was no neat way to handle that."If people say that you achieved something, and suddenly they also say that it's not yours," he recalled. "Pressure was obviously there, probably even much more considering the circumstances."Even when he knew he had to chase the 2500 rating again, the situation did not help him in his game either."Strength was obviously there, but my mindset was not in a perfect state. A lot of pressure and other things happening around it, it was very difficult to focus," he admitted.What helped was a mentor, whose name he chose not to share."Luckily I managed to find a very nice mentor, and somehow he managed to put me on the right track." Asked to name him, Rathanvel laughed it off: "I'd like to keep him secret for a while."The only way to settle things was on the board, all over again. In October, he played the 22nd Chefchaouen International Open in Morocco and won the title there, finishing unbeaten on 7/9 with five wins and four draws.He beat Grandmasters like Deep Sengupta and David Larino Nieto along the way.Round seven, against Larino Nieto, was the one that counted."I knew that if I win against Larino in Round 7, I will be very close to 2500, probably 2499.7 or something," he added. "And they consider 2499.7 as 2500. So I managed to win him, and eventually I crossed it."FIDE's Qualification Commission confirmed in 2025 that rating-based titles can be awarded on live ratings, but it was not obvious that a live 2499.7 rounds up the way a published figure would.Rathanvel's tournament finished with two draws, leaving his live rating at 2497.7.So he kept playing. Last week, at the Dr. Kantor Sandor Memorial in Debrecen, Hungary, he beat WFM Sara Maria Sunea and GM Attila Czebe in the first two rounds. That added 3.4 points and took his live rating to 2501.1, a figure with no rounding argument attached.His norms had been in place for years. The rating, at last, was above the line, and Rathanvel was India’s 99th GM again.Asked how it felt, Rathanvel sighed, "Eventually things went well, and I'm kind of relieved more than a celebration, I would say."Rathanvel waited four years for a number, saw it celebrated, watched it vanish, and then had to go out and earn it a second time. Strangely, the only thing that feels settled is how he feels about it. He is relieved, not triumphant, and for now that is the part nobody can take back.
Article Summary: VS Rathanvel, a 25-year-old from Coimbatore, became India's 99th Grandmaster last July. He had been stuck in the high 2490s, and by his own count had reached the edge of 2500 "probably 3-4 times" His performance ratings in the two events, 2225 and 2299, were both below his own rating.

Article Title: Spanish footballer dies aged 30 a day after suffering cardiac arrest in on-field collision with goalkeeper
Article Text:
Jesus de Miguel (Pic credit: Tenerife)

What happened during the match?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Football fraternity pays tribute

Spanish football was plunged into mourning after Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died aged 30 on Tuesday, a day after suffering a cardiac arrest following a collision with an opposition goalkeeper during a second-division match.De Miguel collapsed after a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during Monday's match, which was abandoned in the seventh minute of stoppage time with the scores level at 2-2. The striker was rushed to hospital after receiving treatment on the pitch, but his condition deteriorated overnight.Tenerife confirmed his death in an emotional statement."Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," the club said."There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness."The club also expressed solidarity with the striker's family and loved ones, adding: "We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome."The incident occurred when De Miguel appeared set to race away on a counter-attack in search of a late winner.As a long ball dropped towards him near the halfway line, Owono rushed out of his area to clear it but struck the Tenerife forward in the chest with his knee.De Miguel initially rolled around in pain before becoming motionless, prompting medical staff to rush onto the pitch. He received treatment for more than five minutes as visibly distressed teammates watched on, with some appearing to break down in tears.According to Spanish media reports, the striker suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance.Owono was initially shown a red card for the challenge before the referee abandoned the match. De Miguel was subsequently carried off on a stretcher to a standing ovation from spectators.FC Andorra offered its condolences following the news, saying: "With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace."The Spanish Footballers Association (AFE) also expressed its "deepest sorrow", adding: "His loss leaves a huge void among those of us who shared his passion for football, his commitment to the footballers' community, and his work defending the rights of our fellow professionals."De Miguel joined Tenerife in 2025 and scored 11 goals in 30 appearances, helping the club secure promotion from Spain's third division as champions. He had previously played a key role in promotions for Internacional de Madrid and CD Castellón.His family thanked everyone for their messages of support and requested "maximum respect for his privacy" during the difficult time.
Article Summary: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel has died aged 30. De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest following a collision with an opposition goalkeeper. The match was abandoned in the seventh minute of stoppage time with the scores level at 2-2. Tenerife confirmed his death in an emotional statement.

Article Title: Kimi Antonelli: A nightmare rookie season, replacing Lewis Hamilton, and the making of F1's youngest-ever World Champion
Article Text:

A difficult rookie season: When expectations became overwhelming

The 2026 turnaround: From rookie to champion

Nine victories that defined Antonelli's championship season

From his rookie season in 2025 to world champion in 2026, a look at Kimi Antonelli's remarkable numbers and the progress behind his rise to the top.

From his maiden Grand Prix victory in China to nine wins in a championship-winning campaign, a look at the victories that defined Kimi Antonelli's remarkable 2026 season.]

Breaking Sebastian Vettel's record

At 20 years and 68 days, Kimi Antonelli has entered Formula 1 history. Here's how he compares with the youngest drivers to win the world championship.]

Kimi Antonelli, the Mercedes protege, has done it. The Italian has become Formula 1's youngest-ever World Champion, breaking the record held by Sebastian Vettel, who was crowned champion in 2010 at the age of 23. Antonelli has achieved the feat in just his second season with Mercedes, having endured a difficult rookie campaign before dominating the 2026 season.Nine wins, 16 podiums in 19 rounds and six consecutive victories. His 2026 campaign was a remarkable turnaround from a debut season in which the pressure of replacing a seven-time world champion often showed.Antonelli's Formula 1 journey took a significant turn in August 2024 when Mercedes announced him as Hamilton's replacement for the 2025 season.Hamilton's decision to leave Mercedes for Ferrari brought an end to a hugely successful partnership that had produced six Drivers' Championships and multiple Constructors' titles. Replacing a driver of his stature was never going to be an easy assignment, particularly for an 18-year-old making his Formula 1 debut.However, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff placed his faith in Antonelli, who had impressed through the junior categories.It was not a decision taken lightly. Mercedes were handing one of the biggest seats in Formula 1 to an 18-year-old, with the added responsibility of replacing a seven-time world champion. Antonelli had won the Italian and ADAC Formula 4 championships in 2022 before claiming the Formula Regional European Championship in 2023. He subsequently moved directly into Formula 2, skipping Formula 3 altogether.At the start of his F1 career in 2025, Antonelli secured fourth and sixth positions in China and Japan, showing that the Mercedes protege could compete with the established names on the grid. But the Italian endured a difficult European stretch, with retirements at Imola, Spain, Austria and Britain, alongside disappointing results in Monaco and Belgium.Antonelli later admitted that he had allowed the expectations surrounding him to affect his performances."I let the pressure kind of destroy me as well during that period," he reflected while discussing his difficult rookie campaign.There were encouraging moments, too. Antonelli secured his maiden Formula 1 podium with a third-place finish in Canada. He later finished second in Brazil and added another podium in Las Vegas. He ended his debut campaign with 150 points and three podium finishes, despite the difficult spells through the season.The first season had given Antonelli a difficult introduction to Formula 1. He returned in 2026 with a better understanding of the demands of the sport and the expectations that came with driving for Mercedes.He finished second at the Australian Grand Prix before producing a breakthrough performance in China. After securing his maiden Formula 1 pole position in Shanghai, Antonelli converted it into his first Grand Prix victory.The Italian briefly lost the lead to Hamilton at the start but recovered his position before the end of the second lap. He subsequently controlled the race and crossed the finish line 5.5 seconds ahead of teammate George Russell.At 19, Antonelli became the second-youngest Grand Prix winner in Formula 1 history and the first Italian to win a race in the sport since Giancarlo Fisichella in 2006.He followed that performance with another victory in Japan, establishing himself as a serious championship contender.Antonelli's 2026 campaign was built around nine Grand Prix victories. His maiden win in China was followed by another victory in Japan. He continued his run with victories in Miami and Canada before adding Monaco to his growing list of achievements.He also won in Belgium, Italy, Spain and the United States, taking his season tally to nine Grand Prix victories.His victory in Mexico was among the standout performances of the campaign. The middle portion of the season, however, was not without setbacks. Antonelli retired in Barcelona and finished 15th at the British Grand Prix.After victories in China and Japan, Antonelli moved to the top of the World Championship standings. Even when wins proved difficult to secure, he continued to collect valuable points through podium finishes and top-five results.By the end of the Mexico City Grand Prix, Antonelli has 380 points, giving him a 119-point advantage over his closest challenger, Max Verstappen, who had 261 points.Lewis Hamilton is third in the standings with 259 points, followed by George Russell on 250.Antonelli's championship-winning campaign included nine Grand Prix victories, 16 podiums, seven pole positions and seven fastest laps.Antonelli arrived at the Mexico City Grand Prix knowing that a ninth-place finish would be enough to secure the championship, regardless of his rivals' results.Starting fifth on the grid, the Mercedes driver faced a race interrupted by a red flag following an accident involving Valtteri Bottas. A late Safety Car period after Arvid Lindblad's crash added further uncertainty.Verstappen eventually secured the victory, with Hamilton finishing second. Antonelli, however, held on to third place and brought his Mercedes home.The 15 points he collected were enough to put the championship beyond mathematical reach.When his race engineer Peter Bonnington confirmed the title over team radio, Antonelli could barely contain his emotions."We did it! Thank you so much," he responded.Antonelli's championship also brought an end to Sebastian Vettel's long-standing record as Formula 1's youngest-ever World Champion.Vettel had won his first Drivers' Championship with Red Bull in 2010 at the age of 23 years and 134 days. Antonelli surpassed that mark at 20 years and 68 days, becoming the youngest driver in the sport's history to win the title.He also became Italy's first Formula 1 World Champion since Alberto Ascari, who secured back-to-back titles in 1952 and 1953.The difference between his first and second seasons was evident in the results. From 150 points and three podiums in 2025, Antonelli progressed to 380 points, nine victories and 16 podiums in 2026.Hamilton's departure opened the door, and Wolff's faith gave him the opportunity. Antonelli has now delivered the championship Mercedes backed him to win.KIMI ANTONELLI IS THE 2026 FORMULA 1 WORLD CHAMPION.
Article Summary: Kimi Antonelli has become Formula 1's youngest-ever World Champion. The Italian has achieved the feat in just his second season with Mercedes. He endured a difficult rookie campaign before dominating the 2026 season. His 2026 campaign was built around nine wins in a championship-winning campaign.

NEW DELHI: Services captain Rajat Paliwal is about to turn 35. He draws inspiration from the persistence of J&K's 41-year-old captain Paras Dogra . On Monday, he was up against Aman Chaudhary - a 21-year-old left-arm spinner - who emerged as Delhi's trump card in just his second first-class game.The word 'relentless' is tattooed on Chaudhary's arm; and on a slow-turning first-day track at the Air Force ground in Palam, Paliwal, with an unbeaten 111, threatened to take the game away from Delhi. But it was Chaudhary's probing spell of 4/79 (in 31 overs) that helped Delhi bowl out Services for 266 at stumps in their Ranji Trophy Elite Group C game.At the end of the day's play, Paliwal, who has 110 first-class matches behind him, didn't want to judge the new-age cricketers who unapologetically prioritise T20 cricket over first-class cricket. He cited Delhi captain Ayush Badoni's consecutive double centuries this season to validate the depth of Indian domestic cricket and then went on to talk about Dogra - Paliwal's "inspiration"."My inspiration is Paras Dogra. He got to lift the Ranji Trophy at this stage and age," Paliwal said, who, earlier in the day, managed to steer his team from a precarious 158/7 to a competitive total on a pitch that's likely to deteriorate.Spinner Harsh Dubey's sensational spell of nine for 53 headlined a dramatic opening day as 14 wickets fell in the Elite Group A Ranji Trophy clash between Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha, with the hosts struggling at 56 for four after bowling out the visitors for 209. Madhya Pradesh, who elected to bat, were bowled out in 66.1 overs on the first day.

Article Title: AIFF bid to break Rs 20 crore fixed deposit to pay Brazil, Uruguay for friendlies stalled
Article Text:
India played five-time world champions Brazil in a high-profile international friendly in Kolkata last month

Panaji:

The All India Football Federation’s proposal to break its fixed deposit of Rs 20 crore to pay Brazil and Uruguay for last month’s international friendlies was stalled by general body members, who said such a move could be allowed only in an emergency.The AIFF invited five-time world champions Brazil and former Word Cup and Olympics winners Uruguay for two high-profile international friendlies against India in Kolkata last month. World Cuppers Panama also played a friendly in Bengaluru. But while Panama have been paid in full, sources said Brazil and Uruguay have received only 50% of their appearance fees.According to sources, AIFF has now sought an extension of deadline to clear pending payments to Brazil (approx. Rs 19 crore) and Uruguay (approx. Rs 4.7 crore) for the friendlies.“The AIFF president (Kalyan Chaubey) requested members to approve withdrawing money from the fixed deposit (before maturity) and said he would later get the money back into the account,” a senior official told TOI on Monday. “Members objected with (vice-president) NA Haris reminding everyone that the executive committee had previously taken a decision not to use funds from the fixed deposit.”Another member told TOI the fixed deposit is from the time of Praful Patel as president (2018-2022). The former FIFA Council member, who attended the virtual meeting, spoke against the proposal to break the FD and was backed by several presidents of member associations.The total amount that is due was not mentioned at the meeting due to confidentiality clauses in the contracts. It was later decided to form a core group, chaired by Haris, where finer details would be shared.“Until the executive committee approves, money from the fixed deposit cannot be utilised to pay the dues,” said another official.Besides appearance fees, the AIFF may also have to return part of the ₹25 crore that was paid to them by the ticketing partner as “recoupable advance.” The federation initially hoped for ticket revenue in the region of ₹30-40 crore, earning them a substantial profit, but high-ticket prices meant ticket sales did not meet expectations.The low ticket sales even prompted AIFF to announce discounted ticket arrangements for supporters of the three big Kolkata clubs — Mohun Bagan SG, East Bengal and Mohammedan Sporting — while a “get two tickets for the price of one with exclusive Buy 1 Get 1 Free offer for the India vs Brazil clash” was also advertised on the federation’s social media accounts.Five-time world champions Brazil arrived in India with a full-strength squad that had Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr , besides Marquinhos, PSG captain during their back-to-back UEFA Champions League titles, Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhaes, Endrick (Real Madrid) and Estavao (Chelsea).
Article Summary: The All India Football Federation’s proposal to break its fixed deposit of Rs 20 crore to pay Brazil and Uruguay was stalled by general body members. The AIFF invited five-time world champions Brazil and former Word Cup and Olympics winners Uruguay for two high-profile international friendlies against India in Kolkata last month.

Australia have named several new faces in their white-ball squads for the upcoming series against England, with young fast bowler Mahli Beardman and allrounders Jack Edwards and Liam Scott among those receiving call-ups.Batting prospects Ollie Peake and Jake Fraser-McGurk have also been included, along with wicketkeepers Lachlan Shaw and Sam Harper. Mitchell Marsh will captain both the ODI and T20I teams."These ODI and T20 matches provide several players, many of whom have had opportunities on recent tours, with a great chance to further demonstrate their ability against very strong opposition," said chairman of selectors George Bailey.Beardman, Peake, Edwards, Scott, Nikhil Chaudhary and Joel Davies have made their white-ball debuts in recent times. India will look to build on their strong start to the Asian Champions Trophy when they face China in their second round-robin match on Thursday. The five-time champions began their title defence with a big win over Bangladesh and will be keen to maintain their momentum against a young Chinese side.India, who recently won their second successive Asian Games gold medal to secure direct qualification for the Los Angeles Olympics, dominated Bangladesh in their opening match. Bangladesh replaced Pakistan in the tournament after the latter refused to travel to India, citing security reasons.The match was largely played in Bangladesh's half, with India controlling the contest. While Bangladesh were not expected to pose a major challenge, India's ability to score from both field play and penalty corners was an encouraging sign.The Harmanpreet Singh-led side scored eight field goals and five goals from set pieces against Bangladesh on Tuesday.Veteran forward Mandeep Singh was among the standout performers, scoring a hat-trick. His return to form comes at an important time, with national selectors expected to assess the players after the tournament.Mandeep was reportedly among four senior players who could be phased out after the ACT.The other three were Jarmanpreet Singh, Amit Rohidas and Nilakanta Sharma.Nilakanta announced on Tuesday that the tournament would be his last at the international level. However, Mandeep and Jarmanpreet are keen to continue playing.Apart from Mandeep's three goals, captain Harmanpreet, Dilpreet Singh and vice-captain Hardik Singh scored twice each. Shilanand Lakra, Nilakanta and Jugraj Singh also got on the scoresheet.India chief coach Craig Fulton was pleased with Mandeep's performance."He (Mandeep) was good, he did full of running and was nice and sharp, which was important," he said.Despite the convincing result, Fulton felt India needed to perform better in the third quarter, after the teams changed ends."We wanted a fast start, which we got in the first quarter. We wanted to play some fast-flowing hockey, which we did. But the third quarter wasn't that good, and that remains a problem. But I am glad we finished strongly," he pointed out.India had to manage without midfielder Manpreet Singh, who has been ruled out of the tournament because of a calf muscle injury. Hardik, Vivek Sagar Prasad and Nilakanta took charge of the midfield against Bangladesh and combined well with the forwards.Mandeep was a major threat in attack, with Abhishek, Dilpreet, Shilanand and Sukhjeet Singh supporting him.At the back, Harmanpreet, Amit Rohidas, Jugraj and Sanjay will continue to shoulder responsibility, while Suraj Karkera and Krishan Bahadur Pathak are the goalkeeping options.India will face a less familiar opponent in China, who pushed Asian Games silver medallists Malaysia hard before going down 4-5 in their opening match.China have brought an entirely new squad for the tournament, with their young players showing promise against Malaysia. Their lack of recent exposure against India, however, makes them a difficult team to assess.Fulton admitted that India had limited information about their opponents."This Chinese team is unknown to us, as they have come here with a completely new group, not the one that played at the Asian Games. We don't know much about them and haven't seen them play. We will have to analyse video footage of their match to get a fair idea about them," Fulton said.India will aim to carry their attacking form into Thursday's match while addressing the concerns raised by their coach. China, meanwhile, will look to build on their close contest against Malaysia and challenge the defending champions.Malaysia will face South Korea, while Japan will take on Bangladesh in the other matches scheduled for Thursday.Goalkeepers: Suraj Karkera, Krishan Bahadur PathakDefenders: Sanjay, Harmanpreet Singh (captain), Amit Rohidas, Jugraj Singh, Jarmanpreet Singh, Amandeep LakraMidfielders: Rajinder Singh, Aditya Arjun Lalage, Nilakanta Sharma, Hardik Singh, Vivek Sagar PrasadForwards: Shilanand Lakra, Abhishek, Sukhjeet Singh, Dilpreet Singh, Mandeep Singh

Article Title: Nagaland United to add a new chapter to Talimeren Ao’s legacy by becoming first club from Nagaland on national stage with IFL debut
Article Text:
NUSC Stadium (left) and Talimeren Ao

On the 107th anniversary of independent India’s first captain, Talimeren Ao, on Jan 28 last year, a new football stadium was inaugurated at the foothills of the Naga Hills in Chümoukedima, and a one-year-old club from the municipality played its first competitive match.Nagaland United FC lost that game 2-3 to Barak FC but wrote a new chapter in the football fate of the state that had given India the skipper who led the country from the front barefoot at the 1948 Olympics in London, carrying with him a nascent nation’s hopes in its first international campaign.And, on a chilly evening in Srinagar on Friday, Nagaland United will continue that legacy, albeit after a gap of 78 years, when they take on hosts Real Kashmir in the Indian Football League opener at TRC Stadium and become the first club to represent the northeastern state on the national stage.“Our aim in our debut IFL season is to build a competitive, disciplined, and fearless team that represents Nagaland with pride,” coach Kaizad Ambapardiwalla told TOI. “We want to compete strongly in every match, establish our identity through attacking football, high intensity, and teamwork, and challenge ourselves against the best teams in the league.”This promotion of a two-year-old club into the second-tier competition was courtesy of another club from the region that stamped its authority at the top tier by winning the I-League in 2017 – Aizawl FC.Having won their first tournament in October last year with the NSF Martyrs’ Memorial Trophy title, the club from Chümoukedima got the chance to face Aizawl FC on June 6, who came calling to their neighbours under the banner of Football for Peace and a “Match for Peace, Goal for Hope”.The visitors won that game 2-0, but three months later, on September 9, the All India Football Federation approved a goodwill agreement for Nagaland United to take a cash-strapped Aizawl’s place in the IFL, as the Mizoram club pledged technical and development support.Taking on the baton from a former I-League champion that has represented northeast for eleven straight seasons in the national league without relegation, Nagaland United will look to add another chapter in the football history of Nagaland, but of the football-loving northeast.“For me, it’s more than just playing at a higher level: it’s an opportunity to give back to the club that gave me my start, represent my state with pride, and hopefully inspire the young players back home to believe that their dreams, too, are possible,” 19-year-old Nagaland United defender Thejangulie Zatsu told TOI.“I know my journey is far from over, and I just want to keep growing, give everything I have for this badge, and make everyone who has believed in me proud.”On the evening of October 30, across Nagaland, people will gather around the screens: in community halls, in living rooms, in shops with their shutters half down as Nagaland FC get the opportunity to add another chapter to the story that started a hundred years ago with a Naga boy chasing a pomelo across a mission playground in the Naga Hills.“As a defender myself, his journey means even more to me because I play in the same position (as Amo). It gives me something to look up to and reminds me that where we come from should never limit how far we can dream,” added Zatsu.Friday will see that dream continue its journey from the foot of the Naga Hills to the Himalayan valley in Kashmir.
Article Summary: Nagaland United FC will play in the Indian Football League for the first time in 78 years on Friday. The two-year-old club will take on hosts Real Kashmir at TRC Stadium in Srinagar. Nagaland will become the first club from the northeastern state to represent India on the national stage.

KOLKATA: Still unbeaten after three matches, despite the frustrating stalemate away in their last game, NorthEast United FC will be back on Friday to continue their winning run at home and stay at the top of the Indian Super League table.“The mentality. We go into every game with the mentality that we are no longer the underdogs,” head coach Juan Pedro Benali said at the pre-match interaction on Thursday.However, on the other half of the field at Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium in Guwahati, will be a side that is also unbeaten in their ISL campaign and sit on the fourth spot having played one game less than the hosts.When NEUFC take on Bengaluru FC , it will be a test of the Highlanders’ defensive solidity – having conceded just one goal in three games – against the attacking prowess of the visitors, led by India striker Ryan Williams.NEUFC were held to a goalless draw by Odisha FC in their previous outing, with striker Alaaeddine Ajaraie missing a stoppage-time penalty, while Bengaluru registered a 2-0 win over Chennaiyin FC through goals from Williams and Mihailo Perovic.Benali believes that the challenge for NEUFC will be as much about breaking down Bengaluru’s structure as it will be about managing their attacking threats.“The details, concentration and crucial phases of the game will make the difference,” Benali added, underlining the fine margins that could decide the final scoreline.NorthEast United, meanwhile, will look to use their own attacking options and vary their approach to create openings. Article Title: 'Enjoying the game has to be the fundamental,' says Tvesa Malik after top-10 finish at India Open
Article Text:
Tvesa Malik (TOI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For Tvesa Malik, a strong performance at the Women’s Indian Open was as much about mastering her mind as it was about getting her golf right. The Indian golfer finished seventh at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, carding a four-round total of one-under 287 (71, 73, 71, 72) to emerge as one of three Indians in the top 10. With Vani Kapoor finishing second and Pranavi Urs sharing fourth place, the home contingent enjoyed an encouraging week at the event.“I think everyone can see it. I’ve always been really proud of how, despite how small the Women’s Golf Association of India (WGAI) started out and how few girls have been playing, so many have gone on to play in Europe and overseas. It’s not an easy standard,” said Tvesa.The progress, she added, has been building for years, with Aditi Ashok establishing herself internationally before Pranavi Urs and other Indian golfers delivered strong performances, including at the Asian Games. The recent Women’s Indian Open, she felt, was another encouraging sign of that development.The emergence of young talent has also caught her attention. Ojaswini Saraswat, who made the cut at the Women’s Indian Open at just 13, offered a glimpse of the potential among the next generation. For Tvesa, however, the key to nurturing young golfers is ensuring that the desire to play comes from within.“A lot of the time, it’s actually their parents who come and ask questions about how they should proceed.For me, it has always been about enjoying the game. That has to be the fundamental. If that is there, the sky is the limit,” she said.She added, “Parents have an important role in helping young players pursue their ambitions, but the goals must ultimately belong to the children themselves.”While younger players today have access to better information and are developing their games at an early age, Tvesa believes they must also learn to manage expectations. The competition is becoming younger and more intense, making it important to balance ambition with patience.Reflecting on Ojaswini’s achievement, she said, “You have to realize that you’re still so young and there’s so much time. Continue learning, ride that experience, and, at the same time, don’t set expectations so high that they become unrealistic.”Tvesa’s own performance at DLF was a reminder of the importance of that balance. The demanding course, known for punishing inaccurate shots and misplaced approaches, requires players to remain composed even when things do not go according to plan.While her ball-striking had been encouraging, she felt her mental approach made the bigger difference during the week.“This year, I felt a bit more accepting of the course. When you play there and you’re from there, the expectations are always high. It’s such a fine line between pushing yourself and almost holding yourself back,” she said.Tvesa, who is familiar with the DLF layout, explained that a single mistake can have a significant impact because of the course’s demanding nature. Accuracy off the tee and precise approach shots are crucial, while missing a green in the wrong place can make even saving par difficult.Her ability to accept those setbacks and move on was particularly encouraging. She recalled how her caddie praised her composure after the final round.“My caddie said the biggest thing was not actually what I had played, but the fact that I didn’t get upset. That impressed him the most,” she said.For Tvesa, patience was the key. Rather than allowing a mistake to affect the rest of her round, she reminded herself that more opportunities would come.That mental adjustment is also central to the challenge she is working to overcome in her professional career. Although she feels her technique has improved significantly, the results have not always reflected the quality of her game.Tvesa, who is married to fellow professional golfer Ajeetesh Sandhu, said, “Your technique is good enough when you’ve practiced and played for this long. Then you have to find the small things that give you an edge. Awareness is a big thing, understanding where I’m making mistakes and why, rather than just spending all my time working on technique,”.Beyond individual performance, Tvesa believes Indian women’s golf needs stronger institutional support to sustain its progress. Drawing on her experience competing on the Ladies European Tour, she pointed to systems in countries such as Sweden, Germany, and Australia, where players receive assistance with accommodation, coaching, physiotherapy, and training facilities.“It’s an expensive game to play, and support is necessary for everybody. Having a team around a player also provides mental reassurance when travel, fatigue, and changing conditions affect performance,” she said.
Article Summary: Tvesa Malik was one of three Indians in the top 10 at the Women's Indian Open. The Indian golfer finished seventh at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram. Vani Kapoor finished second and Pranavi Urs shared fourth place at the event.

Commonwealth Games silver medallist Gyaneshwari Yadav finished eighth in the women's 53kg category at the IWF World Championships on Thursday, while India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu withdrew from the event due to a back issue.Gyaneshwari, 23, from Chhattisgarh, recorded a combined lift of 198kg, with 88kg in the snatch and 110kg in the clean and jerk, to finish on top of Group C. Group A features those with the highest entry totals, followed by Groups B, C and D.The World Championships is among six events in the first phase of the qualification system for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

India will have a 17-member contingent, featuring 11 women and six men, competing across 11 sports at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal from October 31 to November 13.Table tennis player Syndrela Das, badminton talent Tanvi Patri and swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu are among the country's leading medal prospects at the fourth edition of the Summer Youth Olympics, which will be staged in Africa for the first time.Das will take part in the women's singles table tennis competition, while Asian Under-17 badminton champion Patri will represent India in the women's singles event. Desinghu is entered in three swimming events: the women's 100m freestyle, 200m freestyle and 200m individual medley.India's participation will span athletics, archery, badminton, beach wrestling, boxing, equestrian, judo, swimming, table tennis, windsurfing and wushu. The 17-athlete squad will be the country's smallest contingent at a Summer Youth Olympic Games.The 2026 edition will be held across Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly over 15 days. Around 2,700 athletes are expected to compete in 25 sports for 153 medal events. Ten additional engagement sports will also be part of the programme, but will not offer medals.Dakar 2026 will mark the first time an Olympic sporting event is held on African soil.The Games were initially scheduled for 2022 but were postponed by four years due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The previous Summer Youth Olympics took place in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 2018.India have collected 23 medals across the three previous editions, comprising three gold, 16 silver and four bronze. The inaugural Games were held in Singapore in 2010, followed by Nanjing in China in 2014 and Buenos Aires in 2018.Organised by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), the Youth Olympic Games are designed for athletes primarily aged between 15 and 17. Alongside sporting competition, the event features educational and cultural programmes aimed at promoting Olympic values, participation and international understanding.The 2026 sports programme includes athletics, swimming, breaking, skateboarding, beach handball, beach wrestling, futsal, coastal rowing, Baseball5 and Wushu Taolu, among others. Baseball5 and Wushu Taolu will make their Youth Olympic Games debut. Ten engagement sports, including golf, karate and surfing, will be held without medal events.
Article Summary: India will have a 17-member contingent, featuring 11 women and six men, competing at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Article Title: 'Process, routine, discipline': After scoring unbeaten 155 in unofficial Test, Yashasvi Jaiswal shares mantra of success in 'very cold' New Zealand
Article Text:
Yashasvi Jaiswal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

After a brief dip in form, young India batter Yashasvi Jaiswal has returned to scoring runs, with an unbeaten 155 for India A in the drawn second unofficial Test against New Zealand A in Christchurch on Tuesday. Jaiswal said he relies on "process, routine and discipline" to produce consistent performances.Jaiswal said the cold conditions in New Zealand made batting difficult, particularly early in the innings when the ball moved and the seamers found assistance."It's very cold here. The ball moves a lot initially and there is a lot of seam movement. And there are good bowlers hitting good areas consistently. So we have to wait a lot to make runs initially," he said.He added that batting became easier once the ball got older or the pitch settled, allowing him to play his shots."After that, when the wicket gets better or the ball gets old, it's easy to make runs. I won't say it's easy, but you can play good shots. So it was a lot of fun and it feels good to play here. It's a very different experience," he added.The century comes ahead of India's two-Test series against New Zealand, which begins on November 19.Jaiswal said discipline and sticking to his routine were key to handling the conditions."It's not that easy...Just focus on process, routine, discipline. I think you have to be very disciplined here," he explained.Speaking about the challenges of touring New Zealand, Jaiswal said the cold weather was the biggest difference compared to other countries he has played in."New Zealand is a very different place (compared) to India, Australia, even England. Because it's very cold here. If you look at the air, the whole day it was cloudy. Then for some time, the sun came and left. It's been like this for the last four days," he said.Asked how he adjusts his technique to suit the conditions, Jaiswal said he prefers to play close to his body and move towards the ball."Mainly, in my mind, the closer I play to the body, the better it is. Go to the ball and play. If you look at the first innings, my initial stance was behind. Then I changed again. If the bowler is not bowling fast, then you can manage the seam movement."If I get a loose ball, I will try to score runs. Rest is just an effort," he said.
Article Summary: Yashasvi Jaiswal scored an unbeaten 155 for India A in Christchurch. The century comes ahead of India's two-Test series against New Zealand A. He said he relies on "process, routine and discipline" to produce consistent performances.

Article Title: 'They're still playing very well': Mitchell Santner wary of Rohit Sharma-Virat Kohli threat
Article Text:
Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma (BCCI Photo)

Rohit and Kohli expected to draw big crowds

Santner says short-ball tactic may not work against Rohit

New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner knows the challenge his bowlers will face when they come up against India's experienced batters Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli in the five-match ODI series. The first ODI will be played at Eden Park in in Auckland on Wednesday. Rohit and Kohli are now focused only on the 50-over format, but Santner believes they remain dangerous opponents.Santner believes the two veterans are still in excellent form and said his team will need to bowl with discipline to contain them."They're getting on, but they're still playing very well. We saw it in the last series against the West Indies. I've seen it for a long time. I've seen Rohit in the IPL as well," Santner said at the pre-match press conference.The New Zealand captain said his team's bowling plans would depend on the conditions. His bowlers will have to be ready for pitches that offer help to fast bowlers as well as those that provide little assistance."When it's doing a bit, what does it look like? And then when it's flat, what does that look like as well?" he said.Santner also spoke about the excitement surrounding Rohit and Kohli's presence in New Zealand.He expects the two Indian stars to attract large crowds during the ODI series."...I think it draws the crowds. We've had some really good crowds throughout the T20 series, and I expect they'll be the same with Rohit and Virat being here," he said.Santner revealed that New Zealand's bowling group had already discussed India's batting line-up and how to tackle the experienced Indian batters in home conditions."We've obviously sat down as a bowling group and discussed what that looks like, what their line-up looks like, how to operate in New Zealand, which I guess we know how to operate on these pitches," he said.He also explained how Rohit and Kohli could set the tone for India's innings with an attacking approach at the top of the order."Their role is to go pretty hard at the top and then set up a good score in the middle and let their power come in at the end," Santner said."Rohit, obviously, and Kohli have done it for a long time. Shubman's been outstanding as well for the last five years," he added.Santner also pointed out that Rohit has improved his ability to deal with short-pitched deliveries. He said bowlers can no longer expect to trouble the Indian opener by repeatedly bowling short."Teams have tried to go short at Rohit before, but he hits those for six now," he said.The New Zealand skipper believes his bowlers will need to maintain pressure over long periods and make adjustments according to the pitch and match situation."If the pitch offers more than the other night, can you do it for a long period of time and challenge the batter? And then if it's flat, how do we change? What does it look like? Subtle field changes," he said.Santner added that there were no major secrets to bowling in ODI cricket and that his team would have to focus on building pressure and taking wickets."But I think there's not too many secrets with ODI cricket with bowling. It's just building pressure and trying to get wickets through that way."

India leg-spinner Prema Rawat set a new record in the Senior Women's T20 Trophy, scoring the fastest half-century in women's T20 cricket. Representing Uttarakhand against Hyderabad in the Senior Women’s T20 Trophy Elite match at the MCA Cricket Stadium in Gahunje, Pune, on Monday, the 24-year-old reached her fifty in just 14 balls. She bettered the previous record of 15 deliveries, held by Pakistan captain Fatima Sana.Prema remained unbeaten on 50 off 14 balls, hitting six fours and four sixes at a strike rate of 357.14. Her innings helped Uttarakhand post 187 for two after opting to bat first. She was also named Player of the Match for her all-round performance.Fatima had set the previous record in May 2026, when she scored a 15-ball fifty against Zimbabwe in Karachi. The Pakistan captain had broken the previous women's T20 International record of 18 balls, jointly held by New Zealand's Sophie Devine, Australia's Phoebe Litchfield and India's Richa Ghosh.Fatima's knock had also equalled the overall women's T20 record previously held by Marie Kelly and Laura Harris. Prema has now brought that mark down to 14 balls. However, Fatima still holds the record for the fastest fifty in a women's T20 International match.Uttarakhand's innings also featured contributions from openers Raghvi Bist, who scored 72 off 50 balls, and Kareena, who made 44 off 34 deliveries.Hyderabad struggled in the chase and failed to build partnerships, finishing at 98 for eight in 20 overs. Uttarakhand won the match by 89 runs.Prema also contributed with the ball, taking two wickets for 12 runs in her four overs after her record-breaking innings.While the knock has brought attention to her batting, Prema is primarily known as a leg-spinner. She earned a place in India's 2026 Women's T20 World Cup squad after Shreyanka Patil was ruled out with an ankle injury.Prema's selection came after her performances for India A. She took eight wickets in five matches during the team's successful Women's Asia Cup Rising Stars campaign. She had also claimed seven wickets in three T20 matches during India A's tour of Australia in 2025.Prema made her senior international debut in 2026 and has since played seven T20Is for India, taking seven wickets. Her best figures of 3/9 came against Pakistan in the Women's Asia Cup.

Article Title: India-Pakistan 2027 World Cup clash draws 84 lakh ticket requests for 34,000-capacity stadium

The India-Pakistan clash at the 2027 ODI World Cup has received 8.4 million ticket requests, despite the match being scheduled at a venue that can accommodate only 34,000 spectators. The contest will be played at The Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg on October 10 and has emerged as the tournament's most sought-after fixture so far.According to the International Cricket Council (ICC), the match has received 8,397,294 requests through the ongoing ticket ballot. The demand far exceeds the stadium's capacity.The World Cup final, which will also be held at The Wanderers Stadium on November 21, has received 7,900,944 requests, or nearly 79 lakh, making it the second-most sought-after match so far.The response to the ticket ballot has been high across the tournament. The ICC has received more than 120 million requests from fans in 193 countries, with 2.8 million unique fans registering their interest in attending the competition.The 2027 ODI World Cup will be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. The tournament opener on October 7 will be a repeat of the 2023 final, in which Australia beat India in Ahmedabad.India-Pakistan is among the most anticipated fixtures in cricket and one of the tournament's biggest revenue-generating matches. However, India have dominated their recent meetings, winning their last nine encounters. Pakistan's last victory over India came in the 2022 Asia Cup.India and Pakistan are in a group with Australia, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and a qualifier. The other group comprises England, South Africa, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, New Zealand and another qualifier.The top three teams from each group, along with the best fourth-placed team, will advance to the Super 7 stage. The top four teams from that stage will qualify for the semi-finals.Entry into the ticket ballot is free, and fans do not have to make any payment when registering.Each person can submit one ballot entry per match and can enter the ballot for multiple matches across the tournament.The ballot does not work on a first-come, first-served basis. Fans can register at any point during the ballot window, and the time of registration will not affect their chances of getting tickets.If the number of requests for a match exceeds the available ticket allocation, successful applicants will be selected through a randomised ballot process.The ICC will communicate the outcome of both successful and unsuccessful applications through the email addresses provided by fans during registration.

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

IAS officer by day, shuttler by night

Lee Chong Wei 's influence

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.
Article Summary: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. The Indian shuttler lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23- 21, 8-21, 15-21. Suhas has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024.
